column8: User decision 2026-08-14: price 1d through the cost function like the other two arms, not by inversion
column10: DECIDED: 1d is costed the SAME WAY as baseline and 1c -- same cost function, same rates -- with modular_premium_factor as a four-point band on fixed cost. The break-even route was REJECTED by the user because it would make 1d the only arm not priced by the cost function, which breaks comparability. The break-even figure may still be reported as a derived by-product, since it falls out of the same numbers for free, but it is no longer the primary format. Superseded rationale follows -- INVERT the question: set C(1d) = C(baseline) and solve for c_veh_drt_modular. Everything else in C is known -- c_time 33.45, c_maint 0.11, energy from ENERGY_MJ, VHT and VKT per arm. Result reads: '1d breaks even if a modular vehicle costs no more than X EUR/day', and X is then judged against the sourced band for a plain van (Hoerl 14.80, Brotcorne 22.41 EUR/d). If X is far above 22, 1d is robustly advantageous and the missing vehicle price never mattered; if X is below 15, the case is tight and the vehicle price becomes the decisive unknown. This is immune to the objection that the vehicle cost was invented, and Meinhardt et al. establish the precedent for the format

column8: Meinhardt et al. 2022, discussion of freight operator cost
column10: PRECEDENT FOR M11: they state the freight operator 'would not have to entirely account for fleet overhead costs and only pay them partially via a fixed fare per tour, charged by the DRT operator', and that pax already cover part of the fixed cost -- so the true rate is below the base case. That is a TRANSFER-PRICE construction between marginal and full cost, the same question M11 answers with marginal attribution. Citable evidence that the allocation question is posed this way in the literature, and that our answer sits in the accepted range

column8: Meinhardt et al. 2022, Procedia Computer Science, Tab. 2: total = distance + time + fixed
column10: STRUCTURAL VALIDATION, not a number: an independent source builds exactly our decomposition -- 0.2522 EUR/km distance, 17.64 EUR/h driver time, and a fixed cost rate per tour. Same three channels, same shape as C. Worth one sentence in the methods chapter

column8: Hatzenbuehler et al. 2022, Modular Vehicle Routing for Combined Passenger and Freight Transport, Tab. 4
column10: SECOND structural validation and the closer one: their objective is alpha1 * travel distance + alpha2 * fleet size + alpha3 * trip duration + alpha4 * unserved requests. Three of the four terms are exactly our three channels, and unlike Meinhardt this is OUR problem class -- modular vehicles carrying combined passenger and freight demand, solved as one PDP. Cite this for the shape of C. ONE THING TO CHECK BEFORE CITING: alpha3 is labelled 'trip duration' at 6.9 EUR/h, which is the range of a passenger VALUE OF TIME rather than an operator wage. If it is VOT, their objective is a GENERALISED cost (operator plus user) while ours is operator cost only -- then the structural match holds for the operator terms alone. Not decidable from Tab. 4; read their objective function

column8: Hatzenbuehler et al. 2022, Tab. 4, alpha1 travel distance related cost
column10: THIRD distance reference, just below our c_maint_per_km of 0.11 and far below Meinhardt's 0.2522 total. Tab. 4 does not state the COMPOSITION, so it is unknown whether this is maintenance only (then it corroborates 0.11 and Brotcorne's 0.0749) or maintenance plus energy (then it contradicts both other sources and is unusable). Recorded as a lower-bound data point; do NOT move c_maint_per_km on it

column8: Hatzenbuehler et al. 2022, Tab. 4, alpha2 fleet size related cost
column10: NOT TRANSFERABLE, and the arithmetic shows why: at ca. 10 operating hours per day 19.37 EUR/h is 194 EUR/d per vehicle, roughly 9x our sourced capital band of 14.80-22.41 EUR/d. So alpha2 cannot be vehicle capital -- it must carry labour or full operating cost. Against our per-vehicle-hour build of ca. 41 EUR (33.45 driver + 1.5 capital + 2.8 maintenance + 3.4 energy) and Currie/Fournier's 54.7 EUR it still sits low, consistent with an autonomous or low-wage assumption. Their alpha4 for unserved requests carries the SAME 19.37, which identifies it as a penalty calibrated to alpha2 rather than an independently costed item. THE LESSON WE KEEP: a EUR/h fleet term is ambiguous unless its multiplicand is declared -- ours is durH, fixed in vht_basis

column8: Hatzenbuehler et al. 2022, Tab. 4, eta operational cost reduction
column10: THE SECOND SOURCE THAT DECLINES TO PRICE A MODULARITY PREMIUM, and it points the other way: modular operation is assumed 40 pct CHEAPER. DOES NOT TRANSFER AS A NUMBER -- their modularity is PLATOONING (up to Z_max = 10 modules coupled into one platoon, so traction and supervision are shared across the platoon), ours is capsule swap on a single driveboard with one driver throughout. The platoon economy has no analogue in 1d. eta is also their own ASSUMPTION, varied in their parameter study, not a measurement. What transfers is the DIRECTION: together with Meinhardt (premium balanced by energy savings) this brackets the modular premium at 0.6-1.0 and makes 1.0 the conservative end -- see modular_premium_factor

column8: Hatzenbuehler et al. 2022, abstract: 48 pct savings from modularity plus an additional 9 pct from consolidation
column10: FORWARD MAGNITUDE CHECK FOR 1d -- the one number in this paper that maps onto our question. Their 'consolidation' is joint optimisation of passenger and freight demand in one fleet, which is what 1c and 1d do, and it buys 9 pct on top of an already-modular base while empty vehicle km fall by over 60 pct. So the expected order for the integration effect is single-digit to low-double-digit percent, NOT 40 pct. If 1d lands far above that, look for a defect before claiming a result. CAVEATS: 80 requests and 5 depots is a small synthetic instance, their base case is autonomous AND already modular, and the two effects are reported sequentially -- 9 pct is not a standalone consolidation elasticity

column8: Meinhardt et al. 2022, Procedia Computer Science, Tab. 2: Base Case 252208 EUR vs Base Case automated 82598 EUR
column10: Removing the driver cuts total cost by 67.3 pct -- the labour channel quantified by an independent source. Directly relevant to the autonomy switch (BACKLOG / METHODS-LOG 1.1): that is the order of magnitude the switch would move. Their labour share (67.3 pct) is below ours (88.2 pct) and Brotcorne's (83 pct), and the gap is fully explained: their tours run 3.87 h against our 6.71 h, and their 17.64 EUR/h is a TABLE wage, ca. 1.64x below our full employer cost. Corrected for both, the shares converge

column8: Meinhardt et al. 2022, Procedia Computer Science, Tab. 2, driver wages in the Base Case
column10: FOURTH labour reference and almost exactly DHL's 17.20 EUR/h TARIFF wage -- which means it is a table wage, not an employer full cost. The source therefore understates labour the same way the HAGRID legacy model did. Confirms that our 28.99 EUR/h route (table wage plus on-costs over productive hours) is the methodologically correct one, and that the difference is roughly a factor 1.64

column8: Meinhardt et al. 2022, Procedia Computer Science, Tab. 2, all cases fully electric
column10: Practically identical to our diesel build (c_maint_per_km 0.11 + N1-III energy 0.136 = 0.246 EUR/km, +2.5 pct apart) -- good order-of-magnitude validation. NOT directly transferable: theirs is an ELECTRIC vehicle, so the composition differs (cheaper energy, battery degradation, different maintenance). Also a structurally different scenario: 7117 EUR / 0.2522 = 28220 km over 2487 tours = 11.3 km per tour against our 45.7, and 11.3 km in 3.87 h means dense urban delivery with heavy dwell. Absolute values do not transfer, the structure does

column8: Brotcorne et al. Tab. 2, Personnel costs, diesel vehicle
column10: THIRD independent labour reference. Above both of ours: DHL 45539 EUR/a and TV-N 51865 EUR/a employer cost. Over our 1571 productive hours that is 35.7 EUR/h vs our 28.99 (LMD) and 33.45 (DRT) -- i.e. our labour rates are CONSERVATIVE, not inflated. column8: User decision 2026-08-14: accepted caveat, not worth the detail work
column10: CATCH, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. Four sources, four price vintages, none deflated to price_base_year 2026: ICCT 2021, Brotcorne unknown, Hoerl 2025, Currie/Fournier probably 2017. Why it is acceptable: labour stands on 2026 agreements (DHL, TV-N) and carries 88 pct of C, so the only affected cost row is c_maint_per_km (0.11 -> ca. 0.13 deflated, worth 0.35 pct of total cost). The one place it does bite is the Currie/Fournier crosscheck, where ca. +25 pct euro-area inflation 2017-2026 would move 54.7 EUR/veh-h to ca. 68 and widen the gap to our bottom-up from 27 to ca. 41 pct -- i.e. it would enlarge the room attributed to overhead_factor. Acceptable because that crosscheck is a PLAUSIBILITY check, not a calibration: its regressions carry R2 0.37 / 0.11 / 0.06 and the scatter spans 30-360 AUD/veh-h, so a 6 pct rate question and a 25 pct deflator both vanish inside the band. State the vintages in the methods chapter and move on

column8: Currie and Fournier Fig. 6 regression y = 181.47 * x^-0.334 evaluated at a 10-year service length
column10: COST PER VEHICLE-HOUR, which maps directly onto our c_time * VHT structure -- far more useful than a EUR/vehicle-year figure. Curve values: 106 AUD at 5 years, 84 at 10, 67 at 20 (i.e. 64 / 50 / 40 EUR at 0.60). USE AS A BAND, NOT A POINT: R2 is 0.3748, and the Fig. 7 trends are statistically empty (R2 0.11 per vehicle-hour, 0.06 per passenger) -- the scatter is the information, the trend lines are not. Fig. 7 scatter spans ca. 0-360 AUD/veh-h with the mass between 50 and 150. Our bottom-up rough estimate lands near 40 EUR/veh-h (33.45 driver + ca. 1 vehicle + ca. 2.8 maintenance + ca. 3.4 energy at 25 km/h), i.e. between the 10- and 20-year curve values -- plausible, and the gap to younger services is where overhead sits

column8: Sprinti Hannover (Uestra/regiobus DRT): 15000 EUR per vehicle and month, all-in incl. personnel
column10: THE BEST CROSSCHECK IN THIS FILE -- the first reference in the SAME COUNTRY and the SAME MODE. 15000 * 12 / 365 = 493.15 EUR/veh-d = 180000 EUR/veh-a; at ca. 120 vehicles that is 21.6 M EUR/a. FLEET MATCHES OURS: 10 minibuses + 60 Sprinters + 50 BEV, so ca. 86 pct Sprinter class, which is our drt_pax_cap8 -- unlike Berrada/Poulhes, who price a different (autonomous shuttle) vehicle. TWO UNKNOWNS, ONE EQUATION (vehicle hours H and overhead), so it VALIDATES A REGION and determines nothing. At overhead 0/10/15/20/30 pct the implied H is 11.95 / 10.81 / 10.32 / 9.87 / 9.07 h, i.e. 2.1-2.8 FTE per vehicle -- operationally right for 365-day coverage at 1550 productive hours per FTE. Resulting 41-54 EUR/veh-h spans exactly from our own bottom-up (41) to Currie/Fournier (54.7): Sprinti fills our corridor rather than sitting beside it. WHAT IT EXCLUDES: at 16 h/veh-d labour alone is 535 EUR/d against 493 EUR/d total, so a two-shift-per-vehicle operation does not fit at TV-N wages -- hard ceiling 11.95 h. The service WINDOW is ca. 20 h/d (4.5 h night break weekdays, 1.5 h at weekends, Sunday from 08:00), so ca. half the fleet is out at any moment, which is normal for peak-driven DRT. FOURTH TIME OUR LABOUR RATE IS CONSERVATIVE: 33.45 EUR/h is TV-N SACHSEN, Hannover is Lower Saxony where rates are typically higher, which would push H lower still. IT CANNOT ISOLATE c_veh -- do not try: the residual after labour and distance swings 17.95 / 57.55 / 84.48 EUR/d at H = 12.0 / 11.0 / 10.3 h, a factor 4.7, and it still contains the omitted overhead. Sprinti is an UPPER BOUND and a consistency probe, never the source of a rate. VINTAGE: fleet state 2026 with 10 BEV newly added that year; ca. 42 pct BEV share moves the figure by 1-2 pct, and THE SIGN DEPENDS ON SCOPE (corrected 2026-08-14, an earlier note here had it one-directional): Lu et al. 2023 price charging infrastructure at 0.0507 EUR/km, which far outweighs their energy saving of 0.0181 EUR/km, so electrification raises their distance cost by 18 pct plus 2800 EUR/a fixed -- ca. +19 EUR/veh-d, i.e. ca. +8 EUR/d at a 42 pct share. Within OUR cost scope BEV is still the cheaper one, because charging infrastructure is depot cost and therefore sits in the omitted overhead; within Sprinti's all-in scope it is probably the dearer one. Either way the mix effect is 1-2 pct and does not threaten the comparison -- but cite the figure with its fleet state, it will move as the fleet electrifies

column8: User decision 2026-08-14: report direct operating cost, do not pin an overhead rate
column10: ZERO ON PURPOSE, and closed as a research item -- it was TODO until 2026-08-14. WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COVERED, so nobody concludes it was forgotten: dispatch centre (the big one for DRT -- every ride is individually matched, unlike scheduled bus), booking app and matching platform licence, WORKSHOP LABOUR (c_maint_per_km is an ICCT parts-and-materials rate, the mechanics' wages are not in it), depot land and buildings, cleaning, administration, management, service planning, customer hotline, spare-vehicle provisioning. Insurance and vehicle tax are NOT here -- they sit in the vehicle rate. WHY ZERO IS DEFENSIBLE: see the SCOPE block in the header -- an arm-independent factor cancels exactly in every ratio we report, and under all three plausible scaling laws the omission is neutral or conservative for the integration hypothesis. CONSEQUENCE FOR NAMING: the headline KPI is direct operating cost. CONSEQUENCE FOR CROSSCHECKS: every empirical figure (Sprinti, Currie/Fournier, Brotcorne) contains overhead, so our C must land BELOW them -- they are upper bounds, never calibration targets. Also the reason the Currie/Fournier circularity warning still stands: do not back out this zero from the gap

column8: Lu et al. 2023, Vulkaneifel case study, TRA: Electric -> Autonomous columns
column10: RAISED FROM THE USER'S 5-10 PCT ASSUMPTION TO A SOURCED 17 PCT (2026-08-14). Lu et al. allow the clean isolation because their autonomous variant is ALSO electric: comparing Electric -> Autonomous gives +17.4 pct at 40000 km/a and +17.1 pct at 100000 km/a -- stable across mileage, hence not a mileage artefact. It comes from capital +50 pct (1928 -> 2901 EUR/a) and vehicle utilisation +28 pct (0.1579 -> 0.2019 EUR/km) at unchanged energy and charging cost. DO NOT USE THEIR Conventional -> Autonomous figure (+51 to +66 pct): it bundles electrification with autonomy. SIZE CHECK: at 11 h/veh-d non-labour is ca. 125 EUR/d, so 17 pct is ca. 21 EUR/d = 4.3 pct of total -- about one seventeenth of the labour effect. Still clearly subordinate to autonomy_supervision_ratio, but no longer cosmetic. OUT OF SCOPE FOR THE MAIN STUDY -- METHODS-LOG 4.4 excludes autonomy explicitly. The arm is deliberately named autonomy_sensitivity, not baseline/1c/1d/lmd/drt/modular, so an arm filter can NEVER pick this up for the headline results. Applies to vehicle capital, maintenance and energy only (sensors, calibration, remote-supervision hardware); mid-band of the user's 5-10 pct. HONEST SIZE CHECK: at 11 h/veh-d labour is 74.6 pct of cost, so non-labour is ca. 125 EUR/d and 7.5 pct of that is 9.4 EUR/d = 1.9 pct of total -- about ONE FORTIETH of the labour effect. This parameter is nearly cosmetic; the autonomy result is decided almost entirely by autonomy_supervision_ratio. Spend the care there

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THE MAIN STUDY, same shielding as autonomy_nonlabour_uplift. THE DECISIVE AUTONOMY PARAMETER: labour under autonomy is c_time / ratio, not zero. At 1:10 that is 3.35 EUR/h against 33.45 EUR/h, i.e. 90 pct saved rather than 100 pct -- and the gap between those two assumptions is TEN TIMES the whole autonomy_nonlabour_uplift. Meinhardt et al. 2022 set driver wages to 0 EUR/h for all automated cases (crosscheck_autonomy_effect: -67.3 pct total cost), which is the OPTIMISTIC BOUND, not a neutral choice. AND REMEMBER THE SCOPE GAP: teleoperation and remote supervision are overhead, and overhead_factor is zero in this model -- so an autonomy saving computed here is an OVERestimate on two counts at once. Report it as a band, never as a point
